We publish a Go module and are revising CI after adopting Go 1.21's toolchain behavior. There is no workspace. Runner A bundles Go 1.21.3, uses the standard auto setting, and builds a main module with go 1.21.0 plus toolchain go1.21.9; no go1.21.9 executable is on PATH. Runner B bundles the same version, sets GOTOOLCHAIN=local, and builds a module whose go line is 1.21.9. Runner C uses GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path for Runner A's module with the same PATH.

Explain each runner's expected selection or refusal and distinguish the go and toolchain directives, including what a dependency's suggestion does to downstream consumers. Someone proposes GOSUMDB=off to make automatic toolchain downloads work in restricted CI, and claims +path makes the entire build network-free. Recommend a policy without weakening documented verification, and identify any guarantee these settings do not establish.

Starting URLs
- https://go.dev/doc/toolchain
- https://go.dev/doc/modules/gomod-ref

messages.reasoning_content: Let me fetch the two starting URLs.

Both starting URLs fetched. Now let's think about the answers.

Runner A: Go 1.21.3 bundled, GOTOOLCHAIN=auto (standard). Main module go 1.21.0, toolchain go1.21.9. At startup selection: default toolchain = bundled = go1.21.3 (auto = local+auto). toolchain line go1.21.9 is newer than default go1.21.3 → runs go1.21.9. It first searches PATH for go1.21.9; not found → downloads and caches Go 1.21.9 (GOTOOLCHAIN=auto allows download). So Runner A selects/downloads go1.21.9. Note: go line 1.21.0 is older, toolchain takes precedence.

Runner B: bundled Go 1.21.3, GOTOOLCHAIN=local. Module go line 1.21.9. GOTOOLCHAIN=local: go command always runs bundled toolchain. But Go toolchain refuses to load a module declaring minimum Go version greater than its own version → refusal: "go.mod requires go >= 1.21.9 (running go 1.21.3)". So Runner B refuses.

Runner C: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path for Runner A's module (go 1.21.0, toolchain go1.21.9). <name> sets default toolchain go1.21.3; +path allows switching to newer toolchains but disables download fallback. toolchain go1.21.9 newer than default go1.21.3 → tries to run go1.21.9, searches PATH, not found → refuses (no download fallback). Also note: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path — the default toolchain is named go1.21.3; if a binary named go1.21.3 is in PATH it uses it, otherwise "the go command uses a Go toolchain it downloads and verifies" — wait, that's for GOTOOLCHAIN=<name> form. For <name>+path, the +path applies to switching decisions; but for the initial default toolchain name selection, does +path disable the download of the default toolchain itself? Let me re-read: "When GOTOOLCHAIN is set to <name> (for example, GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.0), the go command always runs that specific Go toolchain. If a binary with that name is found in the system PATH, the go command uses it. Otherwise the go command uses a Go toolchain it downloads and verifies." Then: "When GOTOOLCHAIN is set to <name>+auto or <name>+path ... the go command selects and runs a newer Go version as needed." Then: "To run a toolchain other than the bundled Go toolchain, the go command searches the process's executable path ... If no such program is found, the go command downloads and runs the specified Go toolchain. Using the GOTOOLCHAIN form <name>+path disables the download fallback, causing the go command to stop after searching the executable path."

Hmm, there's ambiguity whether +path disables download for the default named toolchain too (when <name> != local and no binary found). The doc's sentence about downloading appears in the context of "To run a toolchain other than the bundled Go toolchain", which includes the default named toolchain case. So GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path with no go1.21.3 on PATH probably fails immediately. Actually the "+path" semantics: "<name>+auto: ... still use a newer toolchain if directed by go and toolchain lines" and path: "searches the PATH ... uses a list of all toolchains it finds" for switches. I think the documented reading: +path disables the download fallback in general (the sentence says "disables the download fallback, causing the go command to stop after searching the executable path"). But the question scenario says Runner C "uses GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path for Runner A's module with the same PATH." Same PATH as Runner A — which has no go1.21.9 presumably. Does it have go1.21.3? "same version" bundling — a bundled toolchain doesn't place go1.21.3 on PATH necessarily. Hmm. The question says "no go1.21.9 executable is on PATH" for Runner A. For Runner C, "with the same PATH". It doesn't say whether go1.21.3 is on PATH. The likely intent: the default toolchain name go1.21.3 is not on PATH either (a typical runner installs go to /usr/local/go/bin and only has `go`, not go1.21.3). So Runner C: default = go1.21.3; needs go1.21.3 which isn't on PATH; +path prevents download → fails. Alternatively, if go1.21.3 were found, then it selects go1.21.3, but the toolchain line go1.21.9 is newer → switch to go1.21.9 → not on PATH → refusal. Either way, with same PATH lacking both, Runner C refuses.

Hmm, careful. But the important nuance: with <name> not "local", the go command "always runs that specific Go toolchain" — download if not found in PATH (for +auto) but +path disables download. Let me just present: Runner C will not reach go1.21.9; default is go1.21.3, and no download fallback exists, so it stops after PATH search. Whether it fails on the default or the switch depends on whether go1.21.3 is on PATH; either way no go1.21.9 download happens, so it refuses (unless a go1.21.9 binary happens to be on PATH — which the prompt says isn't).

Actually, more precisely: Runner C's go line is 1.21.0 (min), toolchain go1.21.9. If go1.21.3 IS on PATH: default go1.21.3 runs; toolchain go1.21.9 newer → search PATH for go1.21.9 → not found → since +path disables download, error. If go1.21.3 not on PATH: error immediately (no download fallback). Both refusals.

Distinguish go vs toolchain: go = minimum required Go version, mandatory since 1.21 (toolchain refuses to load module with go line newer than itself); toolchain = suggested/preferred toolchain, only takes effect in the main module (or workspace) and only when default toolchain is older than suggested. A dependency's go line can force a switch: commands like go get/go mod tidy encounter dep requiring newer go, switch to newer toolchain if GOTOOLCHAIN permits (auto or path), and write new go + toolchain lines. But the toolchain line in a dependency is ignored — only the main module's/workspace's toolchain line affects selection? Let me check: "Only takes effect when the module is the main module and the default toolchain is older than the suggested toolchain." Yes—gomod-ref says the toolchain directive only takes effect when module is main module. And the go line of dependencies is enforced: since Go 1.21, go line of dependency means main module's go line must be >= dep's, and commands switch toolchains for deps requiring newer versions. Also the go line of a dependency acts as a minimum that propagates to downstream consumers (go get updates main module's go line to be >= dep's; a consumer with older go line must update). So a dependency's toolchain suggestion does nothing to downstream consumers; its go line raises the minimum.

Proposal: GOSUMDB=off to make automatic toolchain downloads work — this is wrong and weakens verification. Toolchain doc: "toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification if GOSUMDB=off. GOPRIVATE and GONOSUMDB patterns do not apply to the toolchain downloads." So GOSUMDB=off breaks toolchain downloads (with auto), not enables. Also claim "+path makes the entire build network-free" — false: +path only disables toolchain download fallback; module downloads via GOPROXY still occur; also +path's switch list scans PATH only but regular module fetching still network. Recommend: in restricted CI, pre-provision exact toolchains on PATH (or use GOTOOLCHAIN=<name>+path with goV binaries installed) — or pin runner image toolchain version to satisfy go line, GOTOOLCHAIN=local with a bundled toolchain new enough; keep GOSUMDB on (default sum.golang.org) or use GONOSUMCHECK? Better: use GOPROXY internal proxy (e.g., Athens/Artifactory) and GOFLAGS...; keep checksum DB on, or if truly offline, preinstalled toolchain + module cache/vendor. Note vendoring doesn't cover toolchains. "go mod vendor" covers deps, not toolchain.

Guarantee not established: neither GOSUMDB=off nor +path establishes reproducibility or that builds match the go toolchain's release policy; PATH-found go1.21.3 (or any goV) is not verified by checksum? Actually downloaded toolchains are verified via checksum database; PATH-found binaries are just executed — no verification of their contents. That's a guarantee these settings do not establish: a PATH-found toolchain is not verified/checksummed (the go command does no integrity checking of PATH binaries), and +path means you rely on locally installed binaries; also GOSUMDB protects module checksums, not toolchain binaries on PATH; also toolchain downloads from GOPROXY have checksums checked by checksum DB (unless GOSUMDB=off) — but note toolchain downloads check sums? "toolchain downloads can be proxied by setting GOPROXY and have their checksums checked by the Go checksum database." With GOSUMDB=off, "toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification". So there's a conflict with the proposal: turning it off breaks them.

Another guarantee: GOTOOLCHAIN=auto downloads and runs the toolchain, but nothing guarantees the go toolchain used in one runner equals another unless pinned.

Citations:

- https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#select: selection rules, +path disables download fallback, local always runs bundled.
- https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#download: toolchain modules golang.org/toolchain, checksums, GOSUMDB=off failure, GOPRIVATE/GONOSUMDB don't apply.
- https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#switch: switching for deps requiring newer Go; writes go/toolchain lines.
- https://go.dev/doc/modules/gomod-ref#toolchain: only takes effect in main module.
- https://go.dev/doc/modules/gomod-ref#go: mandatory requirement, minimum version.

Word budget: ≤400 visible words. Need concise. Let me maybe fetch one more page to satisfy "at least two distinct official pages" — already have two distinct: go.dev/doc/toolchain and go.dev/doc/modules/gomod-ref. Both distinct. Could also fetch https://go.dev/ref/mod#go-mod-file-toolchain for the toolchain directive detail (dependency toolchain ignored). Let me check whether the gomod-ref already states "Only takes effect when the module is the main module and the default toolchain is older than the suggested toolchain." Yes. That's enough. But the ref/mod page might clarify "toolchain directive is ignored for modules that aren't main module" — worth fetching one more page for stronger evidence on dependency suggestions. Also could verify GOSUMDB behavior in https://go.dev/ref/mod#checksum-database. I have up to 8 calls; tools available calls 1-7; final call no tools. Let me use call 3 and 4 for ref/mod pages (maybe one fetch of https://go.dev/ref/mod#go-mod-file-toolchain and one of checksum database section). Actually fetching whole page of ref/mod may be huge but fine.

Let me fetch: https://go.dev/ref/mod (whole page, sections go-mod-file-toolchain, checksum-database) and maybe https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#policy not needed. One more page is enough to be safe: https://go.dev/ref/mod.

Then final answer within 400 words. Let me draft.

Decision answer:

Verdicts (facts from docs):
- A: toolchain line go1.21.9 is newer than bundled go1.21.3, so with auto the go command runs go1.21.9, searching PATH first then downloading and caching it. Source: toolchain select & download.
- B: GOTOOLCHAIN=local always runs bundled go1.21.3; module go 1.21.9 > toolchain → refuses to load. (go line is mandatory minimum since 1.21.)
- C: base go1.21.3; toolchain go1.21.9 newer → would switch, but +path disables download fallback and stops after PATH search → refuses (same PATH has no go1.21.9; if go1.21.3 itself isn't on PATH, it may fail there first). UNVERIFIED detail: whether +path suppresses download of the named default; the docs say it disables the download fallback generally; test with `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path go version` and toolchaintrace=1 (Go 1.24+).

Directives: go = minimum required version (mandatory; language version); toolchain = suggestion/preference, only effective in the main module/workspace and only when newer than default. A dependency's toolchain line does nothing to consumers; its go line propagates the minimum: go get/go mod tidy raise your go line and record a toolchain line; consumers on older toolchains switch or are refused.

GOSUMDB=off premise is backwards: toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification with GOSUMDB=off; GOPRIVATE/GONOSUMDB don't apply to toolchain modules. +path only disables toolchain download fallback; module fetches (GOPROXY), go.sum verification, etc., still hit network.

Policy: preinstall exact goV binaries on PATH and pin GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.9+path (or pin image to satisfy the go line and use local); keep GOSUMDB on (or use an internal checksum DB/proxy); for offline, use vendor/module cache, not GOSUMDB=off. Recommend module author keep go line low enough and use toolchain for preference.

Guarantees not established: PATH-found toolchains are not verified by checksum (no integrity check); +path doesn't make builds hermetic; GOSUMDB only covers checksums of modules/toolchain downloads, not PATH binaries; no guarantee of reproducible binaries across runners.
